hints: Look closely at the fast oscillations in Fig. 6.1 - these are the carrier wave. Try counting how many complete fast cycles fit into a convenient time interval like 50 microseconds.
walkthrough:
**Spot the Two Time Scales**
Think of an AM wave as a fast wave inside a slow envelope. The fast up-and-down wiggle is the high-frequency carrier, while the slow rise and fall of its height is the 10 kHz information signal. To get the carrier frequency you need the period of just the fast wiggle.

**Measure the Carrier Period from the Graph**
Count cycles against the time axis. For example, from 0 to $50 \, \mu\text{s}$ there are 10 complete fast cycles. So one cycle takes: $$T_c = \frac{50 \, \mu\text{s}}{10} = 5.0 \, \mu\text{s} = 5.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}$$ Then frequency is: $$f_c = \frac{1}{T_c} = \frac{1}{5.0 \times 10^{-6}} = 2.0 \times 10^5\text{ Hz}$$ That is 200 kHz, much higher than the 10 kHz information, as you expect for a carrier.
Final answer: Period of carrier $T_c = 5.0 \, \mu\text{s}$, so $f_c = 1/T_c = 2.0 \times 10^5\text{ Hz}$.

hints: Recall what an AM spectrum looks like in the frequency domain - it is not a time trace but vertical lines showing which frequencies are present.
The tallest line is always at the carrier frequency you found in (a). The information signal creates one extra frequency on each side of it.

Use sideband rule $f = f_c \pm f_{info}$ with $f_{info} = 10\text{ kHz}$ to place the two outer lines, and remember they should be equally spaced from the centre and equal in height but shorter than the carrier.
walkthrough:
**What a Frequency Spectrum Means**
Fig. 6.2 has frequency on the x-axis and signal intensity on the y-axis. Each sine wave present appears as a single vertical line. For AM with a single sinusoidal information frequency, you always get exactly three frequencies: the carrier itself plus two sidebands.

**Calculate the Three Frequencies**
You already have: $$f_c = 200\text{ kHz}$$ $$f_{info} = 10\text{ kHz}$$ The sidebands are formed by adding and subtracting: $$f_{lower} = f_c - f_{info} = 200 - 10 = 190\text{ kHz}$$ $$f_{upper} = f_c + f_{info} = 200 + 10 = 210\text{ kHz}$$ So the spacing from centre to each side is the same, 10 kHz. The total bandwidth is $20\text{ kHz}$.

**How to Draw It**
Draw three thin vertical lines up from the frequency axis. Make the middle one at 200 kHz the tallest, since most power stays in the carrier. Make the lines at 190 kHz and 210 kHz the same height as each other, noticeably shorter than the middle line, typically about half height. Check they are symmetrically placed about 200 kHz with equal gaps.
Final answer: Three vertical lines: tall central line at 200 kHz (carrier), two shorter equal-height lines at 190 kHz and 210 kHz ($f_c \pm 10\text{ kHz}$), equally spaced about the carrier.
